chapter: The Raeburn band: people and touring
title: Boyd's society-band origins and other leaders turning to jazz
summary: Schremp tells Boyd's background and how hotel bandleaders moved toward jazz in the war years.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: He was born out in South Dakota and he and his brother were raised

on the Plains, like in the television series, and some way he went to the University of Chicago and some way or other, I guess as a kid in school, he started a hotel band, a little society band and I don't know, I've never heard how he got into the jazz business, but I do know that in those days, during the war, during the excitement of the war, an awful lot of people who had hotel bands and tenor bands and nondescript commercial operations, decided they wanted to become jazz people.
Teddy Phillips--did you know Teddy Phillips from Chicago?
No, he was a society-- he had a society band. He may have fronted it by singing, I don't know, but he had a little hotel band like Boyd.
No. I'm thinking of someone else from Philadelphia.
He put together a band not unlike Boyd's band, as a matter of fact. It

wasn't nearly as good or adventurous, but in those days they were comparable. They were trying to do something extraordinary, and who else, Alvino Rey, who had always had kind of commercial perhaps, to say the least, suddenly had a hell of a band and he called his Kenton era Band. You wrote for that band?
There were a lot of people who tried to do that and probably Boyd just got caught up and thought it was a good idea like people got into the uranium business in the seventies or in the sixties.
